subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should an ignore file over 4 MiB terminally hide its directory’s entire subtree from workspace and skill discovery?
rationale: Bounded reading clearly removes the memory-exhaustion path, but the fixed threshold and fail-closed discovery consequence are security and compatibility policy choices that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve terminal fail-closed
options.body: Accept the 4 MiB cap and whole-subtree exclusion as the intended security policy, with the documented upgrade-visible consequence.

options.title: Require a visible diagnostic
options.body: Keep the bounded fail-closed behavior but add an actionable warning or diagnostic before landing.

options.title: Choose another policy
options.body: Revise the threshold or oversized-file response and update the tests and real behavior proof accordingly.

recommendation.title: Approve terminal fail-closed
recommendation.body: Accept the 4 MiB cap and whole-subtree exclusion as the intended security policy, with the documented upgrade-visible consequence.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate for skill-loading and workspace-discovery policy.
